The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages and skin-lightening and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano. According to a statement shared by the agency on Thursday, the interception followed a joint examination conducted at the Skyway Aviation Handling Company Plc Shed. The products were discovered concealed within a 33-carton consignment declared as “personal effects” and transported aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight that arrived the previous day. NAFDAC said a physical examination revealed that “the products bore no NAFDAC registration numbers, while the consignment lacked the requisite import documentation.” It added that “the entire consignment was placed on hold in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service.” Customs target faster cargo clearance Reps to summon NAFDAC, DSS over fake drugs, deaths Onne CAC charges officers to plug revenue leakages The agency said the importer was subsequently invited for questioning and “a statement was obtained as part of the investigation.” NAFDAC noted that the products remained on hold pending further regulatory directives, adding that “their quality and authenticity have not yet been established.” The agency said it continued to strengthen surveillance and enforcement at Nigeria’s entry points “to prevent the unlawful importation and circulation of unregistered, substandard and falsified regulated products and protect public health.” In a related development, the House of Representatives had summoned NAFDAC and other security agencies over concerns about fake drugs and sought tougher penalties for offenders. Christabel Ndoeche
